corrected_coding_set.short_desc: Nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage in hemisphere, subcortical
Klebsiella pneumoniae as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere

code_actions.rationale: No documentation of a subdural hematoma in the CT or clinical notes; imaging/notes describe intracerebral hemorrhage with IVH and hydrocephalus only.
Record documents cerebral salt wasting (and fludrocortisone) rather than SIADH; no documentation supports E22.2.
Exam documentation throughout the stay documents dense right hemiplegia (not left); recode to right-sided hemiplegia and set POA=Y (documented on arrival).

Operative and post-op imaging document placement of a ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VP shunt) - not an intracranial neurostimulator. The billed device code is not supported by the procedure/CT documentation.
Airway protection (intubation) and mechanical ventilation were initiated on arrival; the dependence on ventilator status was present on admission.

discharge_disposition: 62 - Discharged/transferred to an inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF)

evidence.quote: Emergent CT head demonstrated a large left basal-ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with intraventricular extension and obstructive hydrocephalus.
GCS 6 (E1 V1T M4) post-intubation; dense right hemiplegia;
Large left basal-ganglia hyperdense hemorrhage measuring approximately 42 mL with extension into the left lateral ventricle, third ventricle, and fourth ventricle.
Ventricular catheter passed to 6 cm below the dura with return of bloody CSF.
tracheostomy-dependent respiratory status (weaning to trach collar); resolved Klebsiella VAP; cerebral salt wasting resolved;
ABG (02:00): pH 7.29 / PaCO2 46 / PaO2 68 / HCO3 21; Lac 5.7 mmol/L; P/F 71.
Airway protection required with rapid-sequence intubation.
Persistent communicating hydrocephalus post-ICH with IVH; failed EVD weaning trials.
Neuro: dense right hemiplegia with reduced arousal; left side moves purposefully.
Right frontal VP shunt catheter in satisfactory position within the right lateral ventricle.
The course was complicated by acute intracranial hypertension with hematoma expansion requiring aggressive osmotherapy including 23.4% hypertonic saline boluses,
Vitals: continuous telemetry, arterial-line BP, SpO2, ICP; strict SBP target < 140.

system_note: Billed principal diagnosis I61.0 (left intracerebral hemorrhage) is supported by multiple contemporaneous chart entries: the admitting H&P documents emergent CT demonstrating a large left basal-ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with intraventricular extension and obstructive hydrocephalus (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n9, p.72) and the diagnostic CT radiology report states a 42 mL left basal-ganglia hemorrhage with IVH and early obstructive hydrocephalus (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n13, p.136) (evidence: ev_0001, ev_0003). An emergent EVD was placed for obstructive hydrocephalus (Procedure Note - EVD, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n17, p.41) and later a VP shunt was placed (Procedure Note - VP shunt, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n122, p.68), which support the neuro-surgical procedures billed (evidence: ev_0004). However several billed diagnosis lines are not supported by the medical record documentation or are miscoded and require correction: - I97.5 (nontraumatic subdural hemorrhage): no documentation of a subdural collection appears in the imaging or surgical notes. CT and H&P repeatedly document a left basal-ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with intraventricular extension and hydrocephalus; no subdural is described (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n13, p.136; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n9, p.72) (evidence: ev_0003, ev_0001). Action: remove I97.5. - E22.2 (SIADH): the record documents cerebral salt wasting (and its management) rather than SIADH; discharge summary and hospital course explicitly list cerebral salt wasting resolved and fludrocortisone treatment rather than SIADH (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n1078, p.818) (evidence: ev_0005). Action: remove E22.2 (no supporting documentation for SIADH). - G81.93 (hemiplegia, left): charted neurologic exam consistently documents dense right-sided hemiplegia from presentation onward (admitting H&P and subsequent neurosurgery/critical care notes show dense right hemiplegia) (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n9, p.72; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n120, p.68) (evidence: ev_0002, ev_0009). Action: recode to the hemiplegia code reflecting the right side (G81.91) and set POA=Y (documented on admission). - Z98.62 (presence of intracranial neurostimulator): the operative and imaging documentation show a ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VP shunt) was placed and is in satisfactory position (Procedure Note - VP shunt and post-op CT), not a neurostimulator; the billed device code is therefore incorrect (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n122, p.68; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n127, p.234) (evidence:, ev_0010). Action: remove Z98.62 (replace with the appropriate post-procedure/"presence of VP shunt" code only if billed/available - none supplied here). - Z99.11 (dependence on respirator): the record documents emergent intubation on arrival and mechanical ventilation beginning on admission (ED note and admitting exam), so this condition was present at admission and the POA flag should be Y (ED/Admission notes show rapid-sequence intubation and GCS 6) (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n8, p.72; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n9, p.72) (evidence: ev_0007, ev_0002). Action: keep the code but correct POA to Y. Other billed items that are supported and retained: - I61.0 (principal) - supported (ev_0001, ev_0003). - G93.6 (cerebral edema / intracranial hypertension) - supported by documentation of acute intracranial hypertension and aggressive osmotherapy in the hospital course (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n1078, p.818) (evidence: ev_0011). Keep, MCC. - G91.1 (obstructive hydrocephalus) - supported by imaging and EVD/VP shunt procedures (ev_0001, ev_0004). Keep, CC. - R40.9 (coma) - supported by GCS 6 on admission (ev_0002). Keep, MCC. - J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) - supported by ABG/P/F ratio and mechanical ventilation (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n11, p.188; ev_0006) and by intubation (ev_0007). Keep, MCC. - J15.9 / B96.1 (bacterial pneumonia due to Klebsiella) - hospital course and discharge state a Klebsiella ventilator-associated pneumonia treated with cefepime (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n1078, p.818) (evidence: ev_0005). Keep J15.9 (POA=N) and B96.1 (POA=N). - Chronic conditions (I10, E11.9, E78.5) - documented in H&P and discharge; keep as POA=Y. Procedures: endotracheal intubation (0BH17EZ), emergent EVD (00H600Z), ventriculoperitoneal shunt (0016070), tracheostomy (0B110F4), PEG placement (0DH60UZ), and prolonged mechanical ventilation >96 hours (5A1D90Z) are each documented in the procedure notes and discharge summary (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n17, p.41; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n122, p.68; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n1078, p.818; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n11, p.188) (evidence: ev_0004, ev_0005, ev_0006). Insertion of arterial/central access and monitoring device codes (02HV33Z, 03HY32Z) are consistent with the admission orders for invasive monitoring/arterial-line and the ICU course (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n9, p.72) (evidence: ev_0012). Keep procedures as billed. Summary of corrective actions applied to the full claim: remove unsupported codes I97.5, E22.2, and Z98.62; recode G81.93 -> G81.91 (right hemiplegia) and set its POA=Y; correct Z99.11 POA to Y. All other diagnoses and procedures retained. Citations: H&P (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n9, p.72: ev_0001, ev_0002, ev_0012), CT head (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n13, p.136: ev_0003), EVD procedure (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n17, p.41: ev_0004), VP shunt procedure (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n122, p.68: ), Critical Care ABG/P:F (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n11, p.188: ev_0006), ED note (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n8, p.72: ev_0007), Neurosurgery follow-up (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n120, p.68: ev_0009), Discharge summary (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n1078, p.818: ev_0005, ev_0011), Post-op CT (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n127, p.234: ev_0010).
rationale_letter: To: Medical Records / Coding Department Re: Clinical coding review - MR_27 (Neurocritical Care admission 10/19/2026-02/22/2027) We completed a DRG-level audit of the entire coded record for the above stay. Finding: we identified multiple unsupported/miscoded diagnosis codes that require correction. The principal diagnosis I61.0 (left basal-ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with IVH and hydrocephalus) is supported and remains principal. However, several secondary codes are not supported by the documentation or are miscoded as to laterality/POA and must be removed or corrected as follows. Basis for Finding (selected supporting documentation): - The admitting History & Physical documents emergent CT demonstrating a large left basal-ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with intraventricular extension and obstructive hydrocephalus (H&P, 10/19/2026, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n9, p.72). The CT report quantifies the bleed (~42 mL) and confirms IVH and early obstructive hydrocephalus (CT Head, 10/19/2026, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n13, p.136) (evidence: ev_0001, ev_0003). - Emergent external ventricular drain placement and later ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement are documented in the operative/procedure notes (Procedure Note - EVD, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n17, p.41; Procedure Note - VP shunt, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n122, p.68) (evidence: ev_0004). - The hospital course documents acute intracranial hypertension requiring osmotherapy (discharge summary NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n1078, p.818) (evidence: ev_0011) and prolonged mechanical ventilation with Klebsiella ventilator-associated pneumonia treated with cefepime (discharge summary) (evidence: ev_0005). - The neurologic exam across notes documents dense right hemiplegia (admission and follow-up notes), not left hemiplegia (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n9, p.72; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_27.pdf-n120, p.68) (evidence: ev_0002, ev_0009). Corrections to Coding (claim-wide): 1) Remove I97.5 (nontraumatic subdural hemorrhage). Imaging and operative documentation describe intracerebral hemorrhage with intraventricular extension and hydrocephalus; no subdural hematoma is documented (evidence: ev_0003, ev_0001). 2) Remove E22.2 (SIADH). The record documents cerebral salt wasting (and fludrocortisone treatment) rather than SIADH (discharge summary) (evidence: ev_0005). 3) Recode G81.93 (hemiplegia left) -> G81.91 (hemiplegia right) and set POA = Y. Multiple notes show dense right hemiplegia from presentation (evidence: ev_0002, ev_0009). 4) Remove Z98.62 (intracranial neurostimulator). The implanted device is a ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VP shunt) placed 11/05/2026 and confirmed on post-op imaging; the billed neurostimulator device code is incorrect (evidence:, ev_0010). 5) Correct POA for Z99.11 (dependence on respirator/ventilator status) to Y - intubation and mechanical ventilation were initiated on arrival (ED/admit notes) (evidence: ev_0007, ev_0002). Keep the code. 6) Keep all operative/procedural codes listed (EVD, VP shunt, tracheostomy, PEG, prolonged ventilation >96 hours, endotracheal intubation) as supported by procedure notes and the discharge summary (evidence: ev_0004, ev_0005, ev_0006). Arterial-line / invasive monitoring insertion is supported by admission orders for arterial-line BP and ICU monitoring (evidence: ev_0012). Action requested: Please update the claim to remove codes I97.5, E22.2 and Z98.62; recode G81.93 -> G81.91 with POA=Y; correct POA for Z99.11 to Y. Maintain the other diagnoses and procedures as documented above. Documentation references are provided to support these corrections. If you require assistance identifying the precise ICD-10 code that denotes "presence of VP shunt" for device history (to replace Z98.62), please advise so we can coordinate the correct code selection and resubmit. Sincerely, Clinical Coding Audit Team
